Question 1
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=−4(2+t)2, where t is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=2m/s when t=0s, find the velocity (in m/s) of the particle at time t.

a
 v(t)=42+t
b
 v(t)=22+t+1
c
 v(t)=16(2+t)3
d
 v(t)=8(2+t)3+1
e
 v(t)=42+t+2
Submit

decision.explanation: Integrating acceleration gives v(t)=4/(2+t)+C. Since v(0)=2, we have 2=2+C, so C=0. Thus option a is correct.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=-\frac{4}{(2+t)^{2}}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m}/\text{s}$) of the particle at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (-\frac{4}{(2+t)^{2}})\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{4}{2+t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\frac{4}{2+0}+C \\ 2 & =2+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{4}{2+t}.$

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=−4(2+t)2, where t is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=2m/s when t=0s, find the velocity (in m/s) of the particle at time t.

a
 v(t)=42+t
b
 v(t)=22+t+1
c
 v(t)=16(2+t)3
d
 v(t)=8(2+t)3+1
e
 v(t)=42+t+2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we find v(t) by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫(−4(2+t)2)dt=42+t+C To determine C, we use the fact that v(0)=2. Substituting this into the above gives 2=42+0+C2=2+CC=0. Therefore, the velocity v of the particle at time t is v(t)=42+t.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity of a Particle Whose Acceleration Is Not a Polynomial
content.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=-\frac{4}{(2+t)^{2}}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m}/\text{s}$) of the particle at time $t.$
content.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (-\frac{4}{(2+t)^{2}})\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{4}{2+t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\frac{4}{2+0}+C \\ 2 & =2+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{4}{2+t}.$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=8-\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-\frac{5}{2}\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=3\,\text{s}.$
after.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (8-\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =8t-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=-\frac{5}{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{2} & =8(0)-\frac{1}{2}(0)^{3}+C \\ -\frac{5}{2} & =0+C \\ C & =-\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=8t-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{3}-\frac{5}{2}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=3\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =8(3)-\frac{1}{2}(3)^{3}-\frac{5}{2} \\  & =24-\frac{27}{2}-\frac{5}{2} \\  & =24-16 \\  & =8\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $8\,\text{m/s}.$

To determine C, we use the fact that v(0)=−52. Substituting this into the above gives

Therefore, the velocity v of the particle at time t is v(t)=8t−12t3−52.

If the particle has velocity $v=-\frac{5}{2}\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=3\,\text{s}.$

First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (8-\frac{3}{2}{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =8t-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=-\frac{5}{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{2} & =8(0)-\frac{1}{2}(0)^{3}+C \\ -\frac{5}{2} & =0+C \\ C & =-\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=8t-\frac{1}{2}{t}^{3}-\frac{5}{2}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=3\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =8(3)-\frac{1}{2}(3)^{3}-\frac{5}{2} \\  & =24-\frac{27}{2}-\frac{5}{2} \\  & =24-16 \\  & =8\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $8\,\text{m/s}.$
